hints: Look at one node by itself. If both of its subtrees were already mirrored, what is left to do at that node?
Recursion fits well here. Mirror the left and right subtrees, then swap the two child pointers. A queue (BFS) that swaps the children of every node it visits also works.

1. If the node is null, return null.
  2. Mirror the left subtree and the right subtree.
  3. Put the mirrored right subtree on the left and the mirrored left subtree on the right.
  4. Return the node.

approaches.name: Copy into a new tree
approaches.idea: Build a brand-new tree where each new node takes the mirror of the old right child as its left, and the old left as its right.

approaches.name: Optimal (in-place recursion)
approaches.idea: At each node, recursively flip both children and then swap them. Every node is visited once.

explain: Take [5,3,8,1,4,7,9]. Flipping the subtree at 3 gives 3 with children 4 and 1. Flipping the subtree at 8 gives 8 with children 9 and 7. Then root 5 swaps them, so 8 is on the left and 3 is on the right, which reads [5,8,3,9,7,4,1] in level order. This works because the mirror of a tree is just its root with the two mirrored subtrees swapped. An empty tree returns null, and a single node stays as it is.
recognize: When every node gets the same local change (swap the children), a simple recursive DFS over the tree does the job.
